newsitem.title: GERMANY: German minister welcomes EU-Boeing deal.
newsitem.headline: German minister welcomes EU-Boeing deal.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt on Wednesday welcomed a deal between Europe and U.S. aerospace groups Boeing and McDonnell Douglas that sidestepped a transatlantic trade war.
"I am happy that the threatened trade conflict between Europe and the U.S. could be avoided through last-minute concessions by Boeing," Rexrodt said in a statement.

Earlier in Brussels, the European Commission said it would approve the merger of the two U.S. aircraft makers after Boeing agreed to a number of conditions placed on the deal by European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
The most controversial point concerned exclusivity provisions in supply contracts, which European officials called anti-competitive.
Boeing agreed not to form any new exclusive supply contracts with commercial aircraft makers until August 1, 2007.
"The exclusive contracts between Boeing and several American airlines were justifiably described as anticompetitive and unacceptable," Rexrodt said.

But regardless of the concessions made by Boeing, the new company will still dominate the industry, which Rexrodt said made it necessary for Europeans to step up restructuring of the Airbus four-nation aerospace consortium.
"The first step must be a reorganisation of Airbus Industrie from a loose consortium to a unified corporation, at best in the form of a public company," he said.
He added that it was also important for Airbus to expand its product range to include a jumbo jet series to better compete against Boeing-McDonnell Douglas.
